title: The Polite Man
description: The name on the note keeps house eleven miles downriver. Go and look at him, and take note of everything he tells you, because he will tell you everything.

go_downriver.title: Greyhythe
go_downriver.objective: Ludo Corse keeps house at Greyhythe. Go to the Factor's House and speak with him.
go_downriver.journal: Ludo Corse is the factor at Greyhythe. Pyke says he has come down twice in three years, was perfectly civil both times, and paid on the day.

the_chair.title: The chair on your side of the desk
the_chair.objective: Sit down. Ask him anything you like. When you have no more questions, tell him, and he will see you out.
the_chair.journal: He answered the door himself, showed me to the chair, and asked if I had eaten. The chair on my side of the desk is worn through at the arms. A lot of people have sat there, and a lot of people have come to ask him for something.

asked_everything.title: Everything, honestly
asked_everything.journal: I asked what he buys, and he told me. I asked who he buys for, and he told me. I asked about the mark on the note. It is the house mark, he said, and has been since his grandfather. He did not lie once. I left knowing nothing I could say aloud to Reed. He does that on purpose. He has done it to people far better than me. In passing, he said no one has told him what the works at the head of the valley are for. If there is anything to find, it is up there. The goblins in the warren on the quarry road are the nearest people to it who will talk.

asked_nothing.title: Nothing worth asking
asked_nothing.journal: I sat in the chair for a quarter of an hour without thinking of a question that would not make me look foolish. He was kind about it. He said most people find the second visit easier. On the way out, he mentioned that no one has told him what the works at the head of the valley are for. The goblins in the warren on the quarry road are the nearest people to it who will talk.
